title: A protected route admits authenticated requests and refuses unauthenticated ones
iWant: routes marked as protected to serve me when I hold a valid session and to refuse me when I do not
soThat: the middleware boundary is what actually gates access rather than a comment on a handler

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request to a protected route carrying a valid `__session` cookie for a signed-in operator receives the handler's response with status 200 (or the handler's success status for the specific route).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a protected route wired through the middleware with a role gate of `authenticated`
acceptanceCriteria.when: an authenticated request from a signed-in Clerk-development-instance user reaches the route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the middleware runs the handler; the response status is the handler's declared success status (200 for a GET); the response body is what the handler returns

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request to the same protected route carrying no `__session` cookie is refused at the middleware boundary before the handler runs.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same protected route from AC-9103-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request without a `__session` cookie reaches the route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 401 (for an API-shaped route) or a 302 redirect to the sign-in surface (for a page-shaped route); the handler is never invoked; the response body carries no principal or session information

acceptanceCriteria.description: The middleware refuses on expired sessions the same way it refuses on missing sessions.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request carrying a `__session` cookie whose corresponding Clerk session has been ended (via administrative revoke on the Clerk dashboard, or by expiry)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request reaches a protected route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the middleware refuses with the same status and shape as AC-9103-2; the handler is never invoked
